# Cully 0.21.0

- **A starter workflow skill instead of a questionnaire.** The installer and your first launch now install a `dev-workflow-rules` skill at `~/.cully/skills/dev-workflow-rules/` with hint comments in each section and example reference files for codebases, workflow and infrastructure. Cully asks nothing and never replaces a skill you already have. It is linked into your configured agents' skill directories; fill it in whenever you know more. Hint comments are not sent to the advisor.
- **Know what Cully offers after install.** The installer ends with a table of the main commands (agent terminal, advisor, harness audit, agent evals, rescue, replay, handoff, impact and savings, memory, workflow skill, team workspace and update) and points to the skill to fill in.
- **A harness audit that fits mixed projects.** The Instructions check also recognizes `GEMINI.md`, Aider `CONVENTIONS.md`, `.windsurfrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `.openhands/microagents`, so a project that serves several coding agents is not reported as uninstructed. The audit still reads only file names and config keys.
- **A truer panel.** The Git row counts files Git does not track yet (for example `3 tracked, 5 new`), so an agent that mostly creates files no longer looks idle; the MCP row explains that health and authentication stay unknown until the first Cully tool call; and dragging the divider follows motion that some terminals report without a button code, which stopped the drag in Warp even though the divider highlighted.
- **Justify the savings.** `cully impact --explain` shows how the Net token figure is built: skipped advisor analyses times their estimated size, memory hits, and lookup cost, with each figure labelled estimated, observed or measured and a list of what is not counted. Estimates are not billing data.

Update with `cully update --version v0.21.0`, or use the [installer](https://docs.cully.net/installation). Rerun `cully setup` with your original options to refresh installed hooks and skills.

The starter skill grants no access and the advisor remains read-only. Detecting an instruction file does not show that an agent loads it or follows it.
